subject: Bivariate Parallel Process Modelling; Continuous and Ordinal variables

messages.author: e60b4d9c1389d3d1
messages.subject: Bivariate Parallel Process Modelling; Continuous and Ordinal variables
parts:
Respected members, experts and colleagues,

I am looking forward to investigate the dynamics of two concepts repeatedly measured over time. Following are the considerations in that regard.

1. The first concept (say, economic_outcome) is measured by a continous indicator [basically, we have 12 months dataset, and economic_outcome is measured as "income", a continuous variable at each of the months)

2. The second concept is a bit complicated. First the concept is composed of three sub-components, each with ordinal indicators.

For example (only for demonstrative purpose; not the real set of variables): 
The second concept is say, students_cog_ability, with three sub-concepts each measured in 3-level ordinal scale; data collected in each of the 12 months.

 a. attentiveness (0- bad, 1 - average, 2 - good), b. responsiveness (0- bad, 1 - average, 2 - good) , c. expressiveness (0- bad, 1 - average, 2 - good)

There are no missing data.


My research objectives are the following:

(only for example, not the real research question).
a. Investigate the dynamics of economic outcome and student's cognitive ability 
- how do the growth process of economic outcome and student's cognitive ability relate to each other.


My model

I intend to formulate a parallel process modelling. 
I would like to estimate the means, variances, and covariances of intercept and slopes of the parallel latent growth trajectories of economic outcome and students_cog_ability (and/or the sub-components of students cog ability)

I believe that for the second concept (students_cog_ability) and subsequent sub-concepts, I need to construct the 'latent growth curve modelling with polytomous outcome', as also detailed in (Grimm, Ram, & Estabrook, 2017, p. 335)

I am also following the online resources by PennState Social Science Research Institute, who have remarkably preseted lavaan codes to implement models discussed in the book by Grimm, Ram, & Estabrook (2017). The 'latent growth curve modelling with polytomous outcome' model is discussed in Chapter 13 of the book, and the lavaan codes can be found in the mentioned online resource at https://quantdev.ssri.psu.edu/sites/qdev/files/GM_Chp13_tutorial.html.
However, due to the nature of the data used for the demonstration, we cannot really see the lavaan results.


My questions

I would like to seek your expert guidance on the following methodological conundrums that I'm facing.

a. Do you think it is possible to construct a parallel process model with two concepts measured differently (one is measured as a continuous manifest variable;  the other as an ordinal manifest variable), considering my research question?

b. Is it possible to combine attentiveness, responsiveness, and expressiveness into one single concept student_cog_ability; and investigate the parallel process of economic outcome and student_cog_ability?

or, should I do it separately, for example: i. parallel process of economic_outcome and responsiveness, ii. parallel process of economic_outcome and attentiveness, iii. parallel process of economic_outcome and expressiveness?

c. In the tutorial https://quantdev.ssri.psu.edu/sites/qdev/files/GM_Chp13_tutorial.html, the author has included start() function, and provided a starting value. Could you please explain what does this function really do, and how can we determine which specific starting values should we set?

I look forward to your guidance.

Thank you.

Gopal Trital
Research Scholar
University of Pavia, Italy



Reference

Allison Gray, M. S. (2020): Tutorials | Quantdev. Available online at https://quantdev.ssri.psu.edu/tutorials, updated on 7/15/2020, checked on 7/15/2020.


Grimm, K. J., Ram, N., & Estabrook, R. (2017). Growth modeling: Structural equation and multilevel modeling approaches. Methodology in the social sciences. New York NY: Guilford Press.

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: Bivariate Parallel Process Modelling; Continuous and Ordinal variables
parts:
Gopal:

(a) I do not see any problem combining a manifest growth curve with a latent growth curve in the same model.  You will need to declare the ordinal variable in order to include a threshold model for that variable.  In that sense, you will be modeling a latent variable, even though it does not look that way in your syntax.

(b) Combining three variables into one amounts to taking someone's position in a three dimensional space and representing it as a position in a one dimensional space.  If you are only interested in what these three variables share in common, then combining them may make sense (assuming that they have something in common).  If you are interested in what each of the three variables uniquely brings to the table, then combining them may throw away the information that interests you.

(c) Enter your model into lavaan and then try this command, substituting the name of your model where it says 'model'.

>lavaanify(model)

You will get a parameter table.  This is how lavaan represents your model.  If you scan across the column names, you will find a column labeled "ustart" for user start values.  These are likely mostly NA or zero.  However,  you can supply start values in this column and they will override the default start values used by lavaan.  (You can specify them in model syntax, see the online tutorial and model.syntax help file.)  These are the values at which estimation begins.  Specifying them can help reach a solution when estimation fails.  To make you guesses better than lavaan's guesses you want to draw from resources that lavaan does not have, like existing theory and past research.  If the model converges normally from the default start values, you probably do not need to worry about this.  However, you can try different start values just to confirm that you end up at the same solution.

Keith
------------------------
Keith A. Markus
John Jay College of Criminal Justice, CUNY
http://jjcweb.jjay.cuny.edu/kmarkus
Frontiers of Test Validity Theory: Measurement, Causation and Meaning.
http://www.routledge.com/books/details/9781841692203/
